titleEn: Going to the park once a week or more has a measurable impact on a child’s mental health – new study
titleZh: 每周至少去一次公园，对儿童心理健康有可测量的影响
method: Machine reference translation with paragraph alignment; not manually certified.

paragraphs.en: Child mental health issues have been rising in the UK over the last decade. This was exacerbated by the COVID pandemic and continues to be a concern, particularly around issues such as sedentary lifestyles and excessive screen time.
paragraphs.zh: 在过去十年中，英国儿童心理健康问题一直在上升。这一问题因COVID大流行而加剧，并继续受到关注，特别是久坐不动的生活方式和过长的屏幕时间等问题。

paragraphs.en: In a new study, colleagues and I have found that visiting a local park regularly had a measurable impact on child mental health.
paragraphs.zh: 在一项新的研究中，我和我的同事发现，定期参观当地公园对儿童的心理健康有明显的影响。

paragraphs.en: Throughout childhood and through adolescence, children are developing their social and emotional skills. This social-emotional development provides the foundation for good mental health. Failing to reach typical milestones such as developing social skills and friendships provides an indication of a child’s current mental health, as well as their mental health in later life.
paragraphs.zh: 在整个童年和青春期，孩子们都在发展他们的社交和情感技能。这种社交情感发展为良好的心理健康奠定了基础。未能达到典型的里程碑，如发展社交技能和友谊，表明孩子目前的心理健康状况，以及他们以后的心理健康状况。

paragraphs.en: This means that finding ways to facilitate and encourage healthy social-emotional development is a way to improve child mental health and give them the foundation for good mental health throughout their lives.
paragraphs.zh: 这意味着找到促进和鼓励健康的社会情感发展的方法是改善儿童心理健康的一种方法，并为他们一生的良好心理健康奠定基础。

paragraphs.en: Having green and natural spaces close to people’s homes is one factor which previous studies have shown is linked with improved child mental health. These spaces are thought to improve child mental health by encouraging healthy behaviour. For example, they encourage physical activity, socialising and imaginative and adventurous play. Research suggests that being in natural spaces can have restorative and stress-reducing effects for both children and adults.
paragraphs.zh: 先前的研究表明，在人们的住所附近拥有绿色和自然的空间是与改善儿童心理健康有关的一个因素。这些空间被认为通过鼓励健康的行为来改善儿童心理健康。例如，它们鼓励体育活动，社交、想象力和冒险的游戏。研究表明，在自然环境中可以恢复精力和压力-减少对儿童和成人的影响。

paragraphs.en: Much of the research related to green spaces and child mental health has been cross-sectional study designs. This means that the study measurements are taken at a single point in time, rather than following children over time. While these studies are good at discovering factors which are linked to each other, such as natural spaces and child mental health, they cannot determine whether it was the natural space, or other factors that impacted child mental health.
paragraphs.zh: 许多与绿色空间和儿童心理健康相关的研究都是横截面研究设计。这意味着研究测量是在一个时间点进行的，而不是随着时间的推移跟踪儿童。虽然这些研究善于发现相互关联的因素，例如自然空间和儿童心理健康，但它们无法确定是否是自然空间，或其他影响儿童心理健康的因素。

paragraphs.en: These studies also typically measure residential proximity to green and natural spaces, rather than measuring how often children are actually taken to these spaces.
paragraphs.zh: 这些研究通常还衡量住宅与绿色和自然空间的接近程度，而不是衡量儿童实际被带到这些空间的频率。

paragraphs.en: What we did in our study

For our study, we chose to focus on visiting parks, as we thought this was likely to enable many of the ways that research has suggested green and natural spaces could improve mental health. We used data from the Children of the 90s study, also known as Alspac (Avon Longitudinal Study of Parents and Children), where information was collected about 14,062 children born in and around the English city of Bristol from the early 1990s to the present day. We used data on children’s visits to parks, as well as their mental health, behaviours and family circumstances from birth to 11 years old.
paragraphs.zh: 在我们的研究中，我们选择把重点放在参观公园上，因为我们认为这可能会实现研究表明的绿色和自然空间可以改善心理健康的许多方法。我们使用了90年代儿童研究的数据，也被称为Alspac（雅芳家长和孩子纵向研究），其中收集的信息约14，研究对象是20世纪90年代初至今在英国布里斯托及周边地区出生的062名儿童。研究使用了儿童从出生到11岁的公园参观次数、心理健康、行为和家庭环境等数据。

paragraphs.en: We found that children who were taken to the park at least once a week from six months to 11 years old scored, on average, 16.5% better on their mental health assessments compared to those who were taken less than once a week over the same period.
paragraphs.zh: 我们发现，从6个月到11岁，每周至少去一次公园的孩子，与同期每周不到一次的孩子相比，他们的心理健康评估平均高出16.5%。

paragraphs.en: As we had repeated measurements of visiting parks and mental health, we were also able to understand the impact of going to parks on specific children, rather than only comparing groups of children who visited more and less. We found children tended to display better mental health during periods when they went to parks more often compared to when they went less. This provides stronger evidence than a cross-sectional study because it displays change within an individual.
paragraphs.zh: 由于我们对参观公园和心理健康进行了反复测量，我们也能够了解去公园对特定儿童的影响，而不仅仅是比较去公园次数多和去公园次数少的孩子。我们发现，与去公园次数少的孩子相比，去公园次数多的孩子往往表现出更好的心理健康状况。这提供了比交叉研究更有力的证据--因为它显示了个体内部的变化。

paragraphs.en: These findings remained after accounting for disadvantageous family circumstances such as poor housing and maternal mental health, which are known to affect child mental health. The findings were also unchanged when we carried out sensitivity analyses. This is where we change elements of the study, such as what measures we include in the statistical model or which study participants we include in the sample, to see if it affects the results. When the results are consistent across sensitivity analyses, this gives more confidence in them.
paragraphs.zh: 在考虑了不利的家庭环境（如住房条件差和母亲的心理健康状况）后，这些发现仍然存在，这些都是众所周知会影响儿童心理健康的因素。在我们进行敏感性分析时，这些发现也没有改变。这就是我们改变研究元素的地方，例如我们在统计模型中包括哪些措施，或者我们在样本中包括哪些研究参与者，当敏感性分析的结果一致时，这会给他们更多的信心。

paragraphs.en: We also investigated differences in the frequency of park visits for different groups. Children from more advantaged families were taken to parks more often when they were younger, but as children got older this pattern changed. Some children from less advantaged families were taken to parks more often.
paragraphs.zh: 我们还调查了不同群体去公园的频率差异，来自富裕家庭的孩子在小时候被带去公园的频率更高，但随着孩子年龄的增长，这种模式发生了变化，一些来自富裕家庭的孩子被带去公园的频率更高。

paragraphs.en: Many children were taken to the park less than once a week for all or parts of their childhood. Our results suggest increasing opportunities to visit parks in childhood could improve children’s mental health and reduce inequalities.
paragraphs.zh: 许多儿童在整个或部分童年时期每周被带去公园不到一次。我们的研究结果表明，增加儿童时期参观公园的机会可以改善儿童的心理健康，减少不平等。

paragraphs.en: But reducing inequalities in children’s mental health is only likely to be possible if good quality parks are available, safe, welcoming and easy for all families to use.
paragraphs.zh: 但是，只有在所有家庭都可以使用、安全、欢迎和方便的高质量公园的情况下，才有可能减少儿童心理健康方面的不平等。
